feasible.reason: The proposal is realisable on pq1 with firmware only and its load-bearing half (bit-exact per-boot metadata/policy compare + removal of the plaintext fallback) genuinely closes the 'SE re-provisioned with looser metadata in transit' window and converts auth-failure noise into a labelled refusal. All the driver primitives already exist: `optiga::apdu::get_metadata`/`get_data_object` (apdu.rs:958-997), `se050::apdu::get_version_ext` (apdu.rs:944, 37-byte VersionInfo with AppletConfig), `read_object_attributes` (apdu.rs:1042), and a log-structured page-127 journal with `can_append` (512 QWs, first_boot/journal.rs:36,114) where a ~10-QW identity record fits. The plaintext fallback is confirmed exactly where cited (`send_command`, apdu.rs:523-533). The Trezor precedent is real for TROPIC01: `tropic_ensure_configuration` runs at every secmon boot (trezor-firmware core/embed/projects/secmon/main.c:136,139), batch-ID allowlist at tropic.c:784-799, silicon-rev gate at :1007-1023. Cost M / P1 are not wildly wrong (#210 and #206 are already priority:high, and the work is glue over existing primitives). However, three parts of the proposal as written do not hold and must be corrected: (a) first-boot self-pinning cannot detect the stated in-transit swap — it records whichever chip is present at first boot; (b) the SE050 UserID attribute/policy readback is policy-denied on the production UserID (SW=0x6986, se050/mod.rs:834-872), so that leg is infeasible without a UserID policy change; (c) the OPTIGA PRL handshake has no host-random slot at all (shield.rs:386-388 — only `random_S`), so 'add a host nonce to the handshake' is not available, and without a replacement freshness step the per-boot readback is replayable per SE5. None of these is a full bypass of the whole proposal, so refuted=false with corrections.
feasible.corrections:
1. Identity pin must come from the factory, not from first boot. Steps (1)/(2) pin OPTIGA E0C2 UID / sha256(E0E0) / SE050 UID+version at first boot — but the stated threat is a swap in transit, i.e. BEFORE first boot, so the record would simply enshrine the substituted chip. For post-first-boot swaps the pin is redundant with credential binding: a swapped genuine OPTIGA does not hold the DHUK+salt final PBS and a swapped SE050 does not hold the BHK-rooted SCP03 keys, so both handshakes already fail (the bench E2-vs-C2 incident surfaced as an SCP03 cryptogram MISMATCH for exactly this reason). The honest gain of (1)/(2) is a labelled 'SE IDENTITY CHANGED' instead of a generic auth error. To actually defend the transit threat the expected UIDs must be factory-issued (OTP-anchored binding manifest / per-unit receipt, threat-model.md §7.11 'planned binding manifest') and cross-checked by the host verifier (IMP-02) at the box-opening ceremony; the device compares against that, not against its own first-boot observation. Mark this dependency explicitly.
2. SE050 'ReadObject attributes/policy for the UserID' is infeasible under the production policy: silicon returns SW=0x6986 for attribute reads on a UserID gated by the standard two-entry REQUIRE_SM policy (se050/mod.rs:834-872, silicon finding A1 2026-05-28); invariant #2 already records this. Restrict the SE050 leg to: `get_version_ext` INSIDE the SCP03 session (GetVersion is unauthenticated otherwise, #206), object existence/type for UserID/admin/half_E, and attributes only for objects whose policy permits it. Pin AppletConfig (0x3F9F today) and applet version as a FIRMWARE CONSTANT, not a first-boot-learned value — learning it at first boot would pin the substituted variant (same flaw as #1) and #697 still has the production part unconfirmed.
3. No host nonce can be added to the Shielded handshake: Infineon's PRL has only `random_S` (shield.rs:386-388 'there is no random_M'); MasterHello is two constant bytes. Consequence (SE5): a bus interposer that recorded one honest session can replay the entire identity/metadata readback. The replacement freshness step is cheap and needs no PRL change: after `ensure_shield`, issue one command carrying 32 B of fresh TRNG (e.g. CalcHash over the nonce, or a GetDataObject of E0C2/E0E0 with host-chosen offset/length) and require its CCM-authenticated response — only a live PBS holder can encrypt a response to data it has never seen. Without this the per-boot compare is not stronger than a recorded transcript in the pre-rotation window.
4. Do not wipe on mismatch; refuse only. A swapped-away SE takes its XOR half with it, so the remaining chip's half is already useless to the attacker; wiping it only destroys the user's path to a genuine-chip repair and hands an I2C interposer a one-frame DoS via the unauthenticated status paths (SE10: forged bare 0x6986/0x0E already map to PinLocked→wipe; SE11: plaintext `check_provisioned` at cold boot). Any identity/metadata verdict must be taken only from shield-active, freshness-proven reads, never from the pre-shield `open_application`/`check_provisioned` window, and the proposal's 'persistent across two reads' gate is insufficient against a replaying interposer — use the fresh-nonce command instead.
5. 'Refuse on looser' is not a bitmask partial order on OPTIGA. Trezor's `compare_config_strictness` works because TROPIC01 config is 32-bit masks; OPTIGA metadata ACs are expression TLVs (`Auto(F1D0)`, `Auto(F1D0) AND Conf(E140)`, LcsO gates). Either implement a tiny AC-expression evaluator with an explicit strictness order, or ship bit-exact compare against a per-OID allowlist of accepted encodings (current candidate + S-1/S-2/S-3 end state) — the proposal lists both; pick one and note that SE6 shows the installed F1D1-F1D4 AC is `Auto(F1D0)` alone today, so the pinned table must mirror what is actually provisioned, not the documented AND form.
6. Build/platform caveats: the page-127 record only exists on `rdp2-self-lock` builds (production-only), so bench/QEMU images need a compile-time pinned fallback or a skip; the secure slot is already 76,949 B over with ui-px (34 KB headroom without), so the ~3-8 KB of new code + table is affordable but counts against an unresolved flash lever; boot-time cost of ~12 shielded metadata reads + a ~500 B E0E0 read + SE050 GetVersion is plausibly 100-300 ms (consistent with 'few hundred ms'). Classical cert-chain verification stays off-device as proposed; state explicitly that an emulator or interposer that already holds the final PBS/SCP03 keys passes every on-device check — the on-device guarantee is 'the live peer holds this device's final credentials AND reports the pinned identity/policy', nothing more.

vendor-claim.reason: The core precedent is real but mischaracterised in three ways. (1) Trezor DOES run a per-boot TROPIC01 configuration check in production (core/embed/projects/secmon/main.c:136,139 and core/embed/projects/firmware/src/unix/main_main.c:111 call tropic_ensure_configuration() under ensure()), and it DOES pin the peer static pubkey with the chip-presented fallback compiled out in PRODUCTION (tropic.c:383-404; secret_keys/stm32u5/secret_keys.c:80-83 reads SECRET_TROPIC_TROPIC_PUBKEY_SLOT). But the TROPIC check is an *ensure/auto-fix*, not a refuse: tropic_ensure_i_config flips looser bits to the stricter value in the field (tropic.c:615-647) and tropic_ensure_r_config erases-and-rewrites the R-config when it differs (tropic.c:650-677), under crash-safe slot-6/slot-7 journaling (tropic.c:826-842, 950-1004). It refuses only on INCOMPARABLE configs (tropic.c:870-885) or write/readback failure. So the proposal's 'refuse on looser, never auto-tighten' is a deliberate departure from Trezor, not parity. (2) The 'batch-ID allowlist' is not an allowlist: get_expected_tropic_distribution_version_from_batch_id maps known batches to distribution v1 and falls back to v0 for any unknown batch, always returning true (tropic.c:770-782) — an unknown batch is never refused. The 'silicon-revision gate' tropic_silicon_revision_matches (tropic.c:1007-1021) is called only from the TROPIC FW-update path tropic_update_possible (tropic.c:1286-1292, reached via tropic_check_and_restore_fw_update_in_progress / tropic_ensure_fw_updated) and prodtest (prodtest_tropic.c:1522), not as a boot identity gate. (3) The Optiga 'lock-check compares metadata' (prodtest_optiga.c:245-285 get_optiga_locked_status / prodtest_optiga_lock_check) is factory prodtest CLI only (callers: prodtest_otp_variant.c:157, prodtest_secrets.c:109); Trezor's production boot path optiga_init_and_configure (core/embed/sec/optiga/optiga_init.c:47-62) does only pairing handshake + OpenApplication, and on handshake failure it soft-resets and *continues without Optiga* (comment at optiga_init.c:52-55) — no boot refusal, no cert/UID read (grep for OID_CERT_DEV/0xE0E0/0xE0C2 in sec/optiga/*.c, bootloader, kernel, secmon: zero hits). Firmware-side metadata comparison exists only in optiga_set_metadata (optiga.c:311-350: compare, write-if-different, then lock LcsO=OPERATIONAL in PRODUCTION) and runs at PIN setup via optiga_pin_init (optiga.c:720-724, called from storage/storage.c:711), i.e. also write-to-fix, not per-boot refuse. Hence no vendor ships per-boot Optiga/SE050 metadata-and-identity *refusal*; the per-boot-refuse + explicit UID/cert-hash pin + SE050 leg of IMP-05 is beyond Trezor, while the config-ensure and pinned-peer-key parts are parity. 'parity' is therefore an under-claim, not a false 'beyond', so no refutation trigger fires. Two cited sources do not support the claim: arxiv 2608.17082 is 'SentryBus' (I2C sensor-interface manipulation observability for medical IoT; no hardware wallet / SE content, and it explicitly claims no detection rate), and the Donjon Safe-3 page only says a previously known attack bypassed some supply-chain countermeasures (no Optiga metadata content). Repo evidence checks out: optiga/apdu.rs:523-533 plaintext fallback confirmed; SE5/SE10 rows confirmed at secure-element-adversarial-review.md:26,31 (they cite the older apdu.rs:432-434 line numbers for the same fallback); README.md:184, threat-model.md:339-345 and :505-506 confirmed; issues #210/#206/#27/#63/#697/#244/#245 all OPEN with matching titles. PQSigner has a GetVersion APDU (se050/apdu.rs:944) but it is only used by the stress harness (se050_stress/ctx.rs:502, se050_stress/tests/audit.rs:433), never at boot; no 0xE0C2/0xE0E0 read exists in secure/src.
vendor-claim.corrections: Corrected precedent: (a) Trezor TROPIC01: per-boot tropic_ensure_configuration() in secmon (main.c:136,139) is write-to-fix (tropic.c:615-647 i-config bit-flip tighten; :650-677 r-config erase+rewrite; :826-842 crash-safe slot 6/7), refusing only INCOMPARABLE (:870-885) or write failure; batch table TROPIC_BATCHES_V1 (tropic.c:106-107, :770-782) selects a config distribution version with a permissive default, never refuses; tropic_silicon_revision_matches (:1007-1021) gates only the SE FW-update path (:1286-1292) and prodtest (prodtest_tropic.c:1522). Identity pin is implicit via pinned Noise static key SECRET_TROPIC_TROPIC_PUBKEY_SLOT (secret_keys.c:80-83; tropic.c:383-404, chip-presented fallback only under !PRODUCTION||TREZOR_PRODTEST) — the correct 'identity pin' precedent, and stronger than a UID compare since a swapped chip cannot complete the handshake. (b) Trezor Optiga: no boot-time identity/metadata check in production firmware; optiga_init_and_configure (optiga_init.c:47-62) continues without Optiga if the pairing handshake fails; metadata compare+write+lock happens at PIN init (optiga.c:311-350, :720-724, storage.c:711); prodtest_optiga.c:245-285 lock-check is factory CLI only. Replace 'prodtest_optiga.c:173-285 (lock-check metadata compare)' with 'prodtest_optiga.c:245-285 (factory-only lock-check); optiga.c:311-350 (PIN-init-time compare/write/lock)'. (c) Trezor TS7 vuln (trezor.io, reported 2026-08-16): 'proofs verified against a combined key set rather than per secure element; each proof is now bound to its own element'. Repo HEAD (6ab39e95, 2026-09-18) python/src/trezorlib/authentication.py:606-700 verifies Optiga/Tropic/MCU chains against per-algorithm roots (p256/ed25519/mldsa44) and requires identical root, serial and CN across chains (commits 9f72b329d8 2026-06-08 CN/SN consistency; 82ca4a0f37 2026-03-18 ML-DSA-44); the Aug-2026 fix commit itself is not identifiable in this checkout and the vuln page does not name authentication.py — cite as 'trezorlib authentication.py cross-chain root/serial binding (per-element roots)' not 'Aug 2026 fix'. (d) Ledger: Genuine Check is SE challenge-response attestation via HSM; Ledger's own threat model (donjon.ledger.com/threat-model/device-genuineness) states it 'cannot detect unauthorized physical modifications to the hardware, such as spying implants'. Ledger's direction is reversed — the SE hashes/verifies the STM32 MCU firmware at every boot (Nano S; bypassed 2018 by f00dbabe/Rashid, hardened in 1.4.1/1.5.5 per donjon.ledger.com/lsb/002, /lsb/005). Ledger has no MCU-verifies-SE-config analogue because the SE is the root. The rationale's 'Ledger case passed Genuine Check' refers to Kraken 2020 'Bad Ledger' NS-MCU firmware modification being reported genuine, not the flash-drive implant unit (which was a counterfeit device). (e) Sources: drop or relabel arxiv 2608.17082 (SentryBus — I2C sensor-interface manipulation; medical IoT; no wallet/SE content; supports only the generic 'I2C interposer' remark) and the Donjon Safe-3 page (generic supply-chain bypass statement, no Optiga metadata content). (f) Novelty: 'parity' for config-ensure and pinned-peer-key; 'beyond' for per-boot refuse-not-fix policy, explicit E0C2 UID + sha256(E0E0) + SE050 UID/applet-version pin, SE050 object-policy compare, and dual-SE scope — no vendor found (Trezor, Ledger, BitBox02, Coldcard searches) that ships per-boot SE metadata refusal. Suggested novelty value: 'parity+' / 'partly beyond'. (g) Repo-evidence addendum: PQSigner already has implicit per-device identity binding via PBS/SCP03 (like Trezor), but it is undermined by the plaintext fallback at optiga/apdu.rs:523-533 (SE adversarial review cites the same code at the older :432-434); se050 GetVersion exists (se050/apdu.rs:944) but is harness-only (se050_stress/ctx.rs:502, se050_stress/tests/audit.rs:433); page-127 journal infrastructure exists (secure/src/first_boot/{mod,journal,state}.rs).
